propositions: The review-bot container requires IAM authorization to invoke Bedrock Converse API; the existing instance role grants only SSM read + KMS decrypt and must be extended with a scoped inline policy.

The Converse API authorizes against bedrock:InvokeModel (not bedrock:Converse); a policy simulator alone cannot distinguish which action a service checks, so real instance-side calls are the only reliable oracle.

IMDS is reachable from containers on this host (evidenced by opcert's working SSM fetch), so the grant requires no metadata hop-limit adjustment; if AC1 later disproves this, the hop-limit contingency is bounded because all three first-party containers already share the same bridge and instance-role-derived secrets.

The policy must scope to Claude foundation models and *.anthropic.claude-* inference profiles with region wildcards; pinning the region or profile prefix would silently deny legitimate model IDs at runtime (measured for global. profiles in account 896586841071).

Verification requires three independent layers: policy-language simulation, a real Converse call from the instance (to confirm which action the service checks), and a negative control denying non-Claude models (to prove scope actually binds).
This story is IAM-only and blocks downstream story eb6e (Bedrock cutover); it does not redirect rebar's LLM calls or configure region, each of which is a separate concern tracked independently.
